summary: Anthony Robert 'Rob' Yates, 47, of Cortez, caught and buried in a large avalanche (~150 yd wide, snow up to 30 ft deep) on the back side of Shark Tooth Mountain (head of Bear Creek) in the La Plata Mountains north of Mancos while snowmobiling with four others; his sled (buried under ~25 ft of snow) and helmet were found, but darkness and unstable weather halted official search efforts before he was located; family and friends on a private horseback search recovered his body on 2014-06-08
location: Shark Tooth Mountain (Sharkstooth), head of Bear Creek, La Plata Mountains, near Mancos
responding_agency: Montezuma County Sheriff's Office; Montezuma County SAR; Mancos Fire and Rescue; San Miguel County helicopter and K-9 teams; Care Flight; Buckley AFB Black Hawk (HAATS); Colorado Avalanche Control Center avalanche specialists
notes: Date = the Wednesday of the incident per the MCSO report quoted on SnoWest and the victim's Farmington Daily Times obituary (2014-03-05 weekday-verified); slide struck ~1:08 p.m., group rode ~20 mi out from Mancos. Official search (20 searchers, dogs, probe lines, Black Hawk airlift to within 350 yd of the slide) suspended after March 6 due to hazardous weather; MCSO closed the investigation after the June recovery. Body-recovery detail (Sunday 2014-06-08 ~1 p.m., family/friends horseback search from a mid-May base camp) is search-snippet-sourced from the MCSO announcement quoted on SnoWest page 4 — the page itself is bot-walled, verify on a future visit. Resolves the run-147 pending Sharkstooth lead.
